mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing and broader supply activity, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both Real Final Sales (RSAFS) and Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand across consumption and investment channels, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS m/m change < -1% AND HOUST m/m change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above the trend growth rate for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in Industrial Production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1% month-over-month, combined with a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5%, signals an overheating supply response in a tight labor market, which historically precedes profit margin compression and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply surge
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.
